samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` drops non-finite entries instead of zeroing them, shifting later columns' indices and able to produce an empty `columnWidths` — the exact failure its own docstring forbids
samples.evidence: Lines 252-262: `const ratio = normalizeColumnRatio(Number(part)); if (ratio === undefined) continue;`. `normalizeColumnRatio` returns `undefined` for any non-finite value, so `'1e400,0.5'` → `[0.5]` and `'1e400'` → `[]` (asserted in packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts: `expect(colsOf('1e400')).toEqual([])`). `columnWidths.length` IS `numCols` in `computeTableLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:221): with `numCols` short, the surplus cells are never laid out and step 7 never registers their blocks in `blockParentMap` (table-layout.ts:423-431), so their content becomes unreachable rather than merely mis-sized — precisely what the function's own comment says a band may not do ("A band may repair a number; it may not delete a column"). The old open-coded parser kept `Infinity` (its filter only removed `NaN`), so this is a behaviour change from "bad geometry" to "dropped content". The sibling walk `bandBlockNumerics` (numeric-attrs.ts:381) deliberately uses `normalizeColumnRatio(...) ?? 0` to preserve indices; this parser does not.

samples.summary: A non-number `listLevel` in a slide block is silently rewritten to 0 (nesting lost) instead of 400ed, and `bandBlockNumerics` does the same on every read of an already-stored deck
samples.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` does `block.listLevel = normalizeListLevel(asFiniteNumber(block.listLevel))`; `asFiniteNumber` returns `undefined` for a string, and `normalizeListLevel(undefined)` is 0. So a PUT carrying `{"type":"list-item","listLevel":"2"}` is stored as level 0 — silent content loss, where every other wrong-typed numeric in this file answers with a 400 naming the field (`assertValidBlockStyle`, line 411). The same flattening happens on read in packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:344, so decks that already hold string levels (which this PUT never validated before) lose their nesting for every viewer and the repair is written back on the next edit. The PPTX exporter comment updated in this very diff (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts, `listLevelAttr`) still states that such string levels are what gets stored and that its `Number(...)` coercion is load-bearing — the two halves of the change disagree.

samples.summary: Step 5d repairs a `rowSpan > 1` cell's height after steps 4/5c have run, so the repaired cell can be taller than the rows it spans and its content is clipped
samples.evidence: Step 5d (lines 396-411) calls `bandCellGeometry` for every cell, but only re-derives `rowHeights[r]` when the row itself is non-finite or <= 0. For a poisoned `rowSpan > 1` cell the comment itself notes every row height stays finite (step 4 skips it, and `cell.height > spannedHeight` is false for `NaN`), so the `continue` on line 403 fires; the cell is repaired to a real height (e.g. 3 lines + padding) while its spanned rows remain at `MIN_ROW_HEIGHT`. Nothing re-runs step 4's rowSpan distribution or step 5c after the repair, so `sum(rowHeights[r..r+rowSpan-1]) < cell.height` — an invariant the healthy path maintains — and the repaired cell's lines render outside the rows that are supposed to hold them. The new test only asserts finiteness, not that the row fits the cell.

samples.summary: `bandMasterNumerics` indexes `DEFAULT_MASTER.placeholderStyles` with an untrusted key, so a prototype key resolves to a non-style object and writes `undefined` into a required numeric
samples.evidence: `const fallback = DEFAULT_MASTER.placeholderStyles[key] ?? DEFAULT_MASTER.placeholderStyles.body;` where `key` comes from `Object.keys(styles)` of peer-written JSON. For `key === 'constructor'` (or `toString`, `valueOf`) the lookup returns an inherited `Object` member — truthy, so the `??` fallback never fires — and `fallback.fontSize` / `fallback.lineHeight` are `undefined`. The function then assigns `style.fontSize = undefined` to a field `PlaceholderStyle` types as a required number, which the empty-placeholder hint multiplies into a canvas font and `seedPlaceholderBlocks` copies into a Block. The backend's own validator in this change avoids exactly this by using a `Map` (`EMPTY_ELEMENT_DATA`, docs-content.controller.ts:913, with a comment saying so).

samples.summary: Slides table-element geometry numerics (`data.columnWidths`, `rows[].height`, `cell.style.padding`) are left unbanded while the cell bodies inside them are banded
samples.evidence: `bandElementNumerics`' table branch only walks `data.rows[].cells[].body.blocks` and bands nothing on the table element itself; `assertValidTableData` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:945) likewise only checks that `columnWidths`/`rows` are arrays and repairs absent `cell.style`, never the numbers in them. A peer-written `columnWidths: [Infinity]` or `cell.style.padding: Infinity` therefore reaches the slides canvas geometry (`drawTable`/`paddingOf`) unbanded and produces the same NaN/blank render the change exists to prevent, one door over.

verdict.reason:
The code is exactly as described. `parseColumnWidthsAttr` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:252-262) does `const ratio = normalizeColumnRatio(Number(part)); if (ratio === undefined) continue;`, and `normalizeColumnRatio` (numeric-attrs.ts:272-278) returns `undefined` for any non-finite input, so a non-finite entry is deleted rather than zeroed: `'1e400,0.5'` yields `[0.5]` (shifting column 1 into slot 0) and `'1e400'` yields `[]`. The repo's own tests assert this behaviour (packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts:313 `toEqual([0.5])`, :345 `expect(colsOf('1e400')).toEqual([])`).

The consequence is real, not hypothetical: `computeTableLayout` sets `const numCols = columnWidths.length` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:220-221) and every loop — cell layout (:238-269) and step 7's `blockParentMap` registration (:423-431) — is bounded by `numCols`, so cells at indices >= numCols are never laid out and their blocks are never registered in `blockParentMap`; their content becomes unreachable, not merely mis-sized. I found no reconciliation between `columnWidths.length` and the row's actual `cells.length` at the read boundary: `treeNodeToBlock` builds `rows` from the tree children and assigns `columnWidths: cols` verbatim (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:214-241), and the frontend boundary does the same (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480). So no guard elsewhere makes this unreachable.

It also contradicts the function's own documented contract ("an empty array lays out no cells at all, so the row's content never reaches the layout or `blockParentMap` and becomes unreachable rather than merely narrow. A band may repair a number; it may not delete a column", numeric-attrs.ts:247-250), and the sibling walk `bandBlockNumerics` deliberately uses `normalizeColumnRatio(...) ?? 0` to preserve indices (numeric-attrs.ts:379-381) — confirming the intended rule is zero-fill, not drop. Correctness lane (broken invariant / content dropped from layout), reachable from any peer- or import-written `cols` attribute.
